sections.html:
Dane County is large, urban and divided among many taxing bodies, and Madison collects its own current-year tax. The 2020 count was 561,504 residents, second in Wisconsin after Milwaukee County, with nearly 10% of the state's people. Madison is both county seat and state capital.

Housing leans toward renting more than most of the state. In 2020 there were 248,795 housing units and 238,417 households, with 56.3% of occupied units owner-occupied and 43.7% rented. The homeowner vacancy rate was 0.8% and the rental vacancy rate 3.9%.

Municipalities include:

  • Cities: Fitchburg, Madison, Middleton, Monona, Stoughton, Sun Prairie, Verona and Edgerton (mostly in Rock County).
  • Villages: Belleville, Black Earth, Blue Mounds, Brooklyn, Cambridge, Cottage Grove, Cross Plains, Dane, Deerfield, DeForest, Maple Bluff, Marshall, Mazomanie, McFarland, Mount Horeb, Oregon, Rockdale, Shorewood Hills, Waunakee and Windsor.
  • Many towns, from Albion and Berry to Westport and York, each with a board and assessor of its own.

The first payment is due January 31 and the final one July 31. Municipalities mail bills on the third Monday of December, the same day Access Dane is updated with the new tax data.

The yearly cycle runs like this. Assessors set values as of January 1, taxing districts adopt budgets in the fall, and in December each assessment is multiplied by the mill rate to get total tax. The lottery credit and first dollar credit come off to give net property tax, and special assessments and special charges are added to produce the bill.

DateEventPay to
January 1Municipal assessor determines valuesNone
Spring or summerNotice of Assessment, Open Book, then Board of ReviewLocal clerk and assessor
Third Monday of DecemberBills mailed by the local municipalityNone
January 31First due dateLocal municipality
July 31Final due dateDane County Treasurer, except City of Madison properties

Owners pay at different times: roughly 30% in full in December, 40% in full in January and 30% in installments. Madison works differently, with intermediate installments and the City Treasurer collecting through July 31. The Madison treasurer is at 210 Martin Luther King Jr Blvd, Room 107, phone (608) 266-4771.

A missed payment makes the entire bill due at once, and interest and penalty together of 1.5% of the unpaid principal are added back to February 1. The charge accrues at the start of each month until everything is paid.

Someone late on the final installment still owes the charge reaching back to February 1. A payment in August therefore carries seven months of it, and each later month adds another 1.5%.

The postmark decides timeliness, and the Postal Service does not postmark mail the day it is dropped off. Near a deadline you have these options:

  • Pay in person at the City-County Building, Room 114, 210 Martin Luther King Jr Blvd, Madison. Hours are 8:00 to 4:00 Monday through Friday, holidays excluded, and there is a drop box.
  • Pay by e-Check or credit card on the Treasurer's website.
  • Mail a check to Dane County Treasurer, PO Box 1299, Madison, WI 53701-1299, early enough to be postmarked on time.
  • If you pay through your bank, schedule it 7 to 10 business days ahead.

Delinquent tax needs its own check made out to Dane County. A payment is not final until it clears the bank, and a returned payment cancels the bills it covered.

Begin with a conversation with your municipal assessor. If you still disagree, take it to the municipal Board of Review. Once that board has acted, it is normally too late to contest the value for that year.

The Notice of Assessment generally shows up in March or later. During the Open Book period you can go over the numbers with the assessor. Formal appeals are heard by the Board of Review in a quasi-judicial setting, under rules in Wisconsin Statute 70.47:

  • The board meets in the 45 days after the fourth Monday of April.
  • Give notice at least 48 hours ahead, then file a written objection in the first two hours of the opening meeting, unless the board waives the rule.
  • An owner who turned down the assessor's reasonable certified-mail request to view the exterior cannot appear.
  • For income-method properties, send the assessor the income and expense data requested no later than 7 days before the first meeting.
  • If the board waives its hearing, you have 60 days from the notice of waiver to start an excessive assessment action under Statute 74.37(3)(d).

The treasurer's page links the Department of Revenue Guide for Property Owners and the Board of Review Member Guide. Every city, village and town runs its own board, so the local clerk gives you the date.

sections.h2: Parcels that went to tax deed
sections.html:
A former owner can buy the property back before the public auction, and the county sells what it took as is. Dane County does not sell tax deeds or tax liens. It sells properties it acquired through the tax deed process under Wisconsin Statute 75.35.

Auctions usually take place in October or November, and sometimes again in April or May, by sealed bid. Bids are due on a Tuesday at 1:00 pm and opened the next day at 10:00 am in the Treasurer's office. Each bid needs a form and a 10% earnest deposit, payment is cash or cashier's check only, and the buyer has ten days after the award notice to close.

Former owners can repurchase up to two weeks before the bid due date. If the parcel sells at auction, the county returns any net proceeds to the former owner. Occupants may still be living in a parcel at the time of a fall auction, and the county notes occupant status for each parcel. The Treasurer's office asks people not to phone for sale details, so read the Tax Deed Auction page first.

Confirm the balance with the correct treasurer, pay it at closing, and record the deed with the transfer return. Who you call depends on where the house is, since a Madison parcel and one in Sun Prairie or Verona follow different routes.

  • Locate the parcel number on the tax bill, or search Access Dane by address.
  • For Madison parcels, call the City of Madison Treasurer. For others, ask the local municipal treasurer about tax due through January 31, and the Dane County Treasurer about the July 31 installment and any delinquent tax.
  • Record the deed at the Register of Deeds, phone (608) 266-4141, with the electronic Wisconsin Real Estate Transfer Return. The fee is 30 cents per $100 of value under Statute 77.22(1), paid by the grantor.
  • After closing, update the mailing address in writing with Dane County Planning and Development, Property Listing, Room 116, or by email to property.listing@danecounty.gov.

If an owner has died, the name comes off the record by a recorded Termination of Decedent's Interest for joint tenancy or survivorship marital property, or a Final Judgment for tenants in common. A transfer by will, descent or survivorship is exempt from the transfer fee under Statute 77.25(11). A cash buyer skips the lender, but the tax payoff still happens at closing.

faqs.q: When are Dane County property taxes due?
faqs.a: January 31 is the first due date and July 31 the final one. January payments go to your municipality and July payments to the Dane County Treasurer, except City of Madison properties, which the City Treasurer collects through July 31.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to late Dane County property tax?
faqs.a: Interest and penalty combined come to 1.5% of unpaid principal per month, added back to February 1. A missed installment makes the full amount due, and a payment in August carries seven months of the charge.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Dane County property tax in person?
faqs.a: At the Dane County Treasurer's office in the City-County Building, Room 114, 210 Martin Luther King Jr Blvd, Madison. It is open 8:00 to 4:00 Monday through Friday, holidays excluded, and has a drop box.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Dane County assessment after the Board of Review?
faqs.a: Usually not for that year. After the Board of Review it would normally be too late. Talk to your assessor during the Open Book period and file with the board on time.

faqs.q: How do I change the billing address on a Dane County parcel?
faqs.a: Contact the municipal clerk or treasurer, or write to Dane County Planning and Development, Property Listing, Room 116, 210 Martin Luther King Jr Blvd, Madison, WI 53703. Email to property.listing@danecounty.gov also works.
